description: Update docs/architecture.md to be consistent with the new README. Depends on FEAT-001 (must read the new README to ensure consistency).
steps: Read context.json for project context — do NOT re-explore the codebase.
Read the newly written README.md (from FEAT-001) to understand the new structure, diagram, and honesty tiers.
Read the existing docs/architecture.md to understand its current structure and content.
Update docs/architecture.md with the following changes:
UPDATE 1 — Overview: Replace the opening overview to match the new README opening. Remove the 'Phases 1-11 complete' language and replace with honest capability tiers.

UPDATE 2 — System Diagram: Replace the existing ASCII art diagram with a valid Mermaid flowchart. This can be the same diagram from the README or a more detailed version showing internal module relationships. Must be valid Mermaid that renders on GitHub.

UPDATE 3 — Add honesty annotations throughout: For each phase section, add a brief note at the top indicating whether that capability is 'Implemented and tested', 'Simulated adapters only', or 'Prototype'. For example, Phase 11 Physical Robot Support should note 'SimulatedRobot only — no physical robot drivers exist in the codebase.'
UPDATE 4 — Fleet & OTA section (Phase 10): Add a note that all operations are local file-based simulations, no network calls or real device communication.
UPDATE 5 — Phase 11 section: Explicitly state that only SimulatedRobot implements RobotInterface. The safety system is a software monitoring layer. Sim-to-real utilities operate on synthetic data.
UPDATE 6 — Edge Deployment section (Phase 9): Note that TensorRT path is prototype-only (never installed in CI). ONNX path is tested.
UPDATE 7 — Add a Limitations section at the end consistent with the README's Limitations and Roadmap section.
Keep all the detailed per-phase technical documentation (API tables, code blocks, CLI examples) — these are valuable. Only add honesty context and update the overview/diagram.
Ensure all claims in architecture.md are consistent with the README — no contradictions between the two files.
acceptance_criteria: docs/architecture.md exists and is valid markdown
The overview section is consistent with the new README opening
A Mermaid diagram replaces or supplements the ASCII art diagram
Each phase section has a brief honesty annotation (tested / simulated / prototype)
Phase 11 explicitly states SimulatedRobot is the only implementation
Phase 10 notes that fleet/OTA operations are local simulations
A Limitations section exists at the end
No contradictions between README.md and docs/architecture.md
Running 'python3 -m pytest tests/ -v' still passes all 384 tests
verification: python3 -m pytest tests/ -v — all 384 tests pass (documentation-only change should not affect tests)
findings: Updated docs/architecture.md: replaced ASCII diagram with two Mermaid diagrams (pipeline + internal modules), rewrote overview to match README opening with implementation status table, added honesty annotations to all 11 phase sections, added explicit notes for Phase 9 (TensorRT prototype), Phase 10 (local file-based simulations), Phase 11 (SimulatedRobot only, software safety, synthetic data), and added Limitations section at end with JSON storage, hardware, safety scope, TensorRT subsections plus roadmap. All 384 tests pass.
